name: Duke Energy
tagline: Leading energy company providing reliable and affordable electricity to 8.7 million customers across the Southeast and Midwest
hero_kpi_rationale: Duke Energy dessert 8,7 millions de clients électricité dans 6 États du Sud-Est et du Midwest sur un territoire d'environ 90 000 miles carrés. C'est l'indicateur le plus suivi de l'échelle et du leadership du groupe en tant que fournisseur régulé.

kpis.signal: Base clients electricite en croissance reguliere, moteur du business regule.
Base clients electricite en croissance reguliere, moteur du business regule.
Base clients gaz naturel stable autour de 1,6-1,8 million.
Capacite de production installee en hausse avec le plan d'investissement massif.
Demande contractee IA et industrie avancee securisee sous Electric Service Agreements, moteur de croissance.
Plan d'investissement record de 103 Md$ sur 5 ans, le plus gros programme entierement regule du secteur, socle de la croissance du benefice.
Pipeline avance haute confiance de 15,4 GW de grandes charges data centers, gage de croissance de la demande jusqu'a la prochaine decennie.

kpis.short: Consecutive years of quarterly cash dividend
kpis.signal: 100e annee consecutive de versement d'un dividende trimestriel, jalon rare qui ancre la fiabilite du profil de rendement.

kpis.short: Annual nuclear tax credits returned to customers
kpis.name_fr: Credits d'impot nucleaire reverses aux clients
kpis.signal: Pres de 600 M$ par an de credits d'impot nucleaire reverses aux clients, levier d'abordabilite tire de la plus grande flotte reglementee du pays.
Fusion des deux utilities des Carolines validee, avec 2,3 Md$ d'economies clients estimees jusqu'en 2040, effective au 1er janvier 2027.
Plus de 5 Md$ de produits encaisses (Brookfield 2,8 Md$ sur la Floride, Piedmont Tennessee vendu 2,5 Md$ a Spire), renforcant le bilan pour financer le plan.

kpis.short: Incremental generation added over five years
kpis.name_fr: Capacite de production ajoutee sur 5 ans
kpis.signal: Environ 14 GW de capacite incrementale ajoutes sur cinq ans, dont 5 GW de gaz naturel deja en construction, pour repondre a la croissance des charges.
Environ 4,5 GW de stockage batterie ajoutes d'ici 2031, dont la plus grande installation a ce jour (100 MW en Caroline du Nord), soutenant la fiabilite systeme.

kpis.name_fr: Recuperation et titrisation des couts de tempete
kpis.signal: Pres de 3 Md$ de couts de tempete recuperes et titrises en 2025, cle de l'amelioration du FFO sur dette a 14,8%.

kpis.short: Data center share of Carolinas economic development load growth
kpis.name_fr: Part data centers dans la croissance de charge Carolines
kpis.signal: Les data centers representeront 75% de la croissance de charge de developpement economique des Carolines d'ici 2030, contre 50% quelques trimestres plus tot.
Duke prevoit de deployer entre 200 et 220 Md$ dans ses activites regulees sur la prochaine decennie, socle de croissance porte par la demande d'electricite.

kpis.name_fr: Campus IA Amazon en Caroline du Nord
kpis.signal: Amazon prevoit 10 Md$ pour un campus cloud et IA en Caroline du Nord, projet phare de la demande hyperscale sur le reseau Duke.

kpis.short: New natural gas generation in pipeline
kpis.signal: Environ 7 500 MW de nouvelle production gaz en construction ou en approbation reglementaire pour repondre a la croissance de la demande.
Recuperation approuvee d'environ 1,1 Md$ de couts de tempetes en Floride sur 12 mois des mars 2025, apres une saison cyclonique 2024 severe.

risks.title: Government Policy Dependence
risks.score_rationale: Federal or state policies could be enacted that restrict the availability of and increase the costs associated with fuels or generation technologies such as natural gas or nuclear power that enable Duke Energy to reduce its carbon emissions. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "Duke Energy is subject to business, policy, regulatory, technology, economic and competitive uncertainties and contingencies". Position: haut Item 1A.
risks.summary: Government policies can impact Duke Energy's energy strategy and cost structure

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy is subject to regulation by FERC and state utility regulatory agencies which have jurisdiction over rates and investment recovery. Regulatory decisions can materially impact operating results. (Item 1A, Item 4) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "REGULATORY, LEGISLATIVE AND LEGAL RISKS The Duke Energy Registrants’ regulated utility revenues, earnings and results". Position: haut Item 1A.
risks.summary: Regulators can limit Duke Energy's ability to recover costs through rate mechanisms

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: Increased competition in the energy sector may impact Duke Energy's operating results and market share across its service territories. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "Increased competition resulting from deregulation or restructuring legislation could have a significant adverse impact on". Position: haut Item 1A.
risks.summary: Competition can reduce Duke Energy's market share in key regions

risks.title: Environmental and Climate Risks
risks.score_rationale: Environmental regulations can increase operating costs. Duke Energy must manage coal-fired facility retirements, replacement generation availability, and comply with emission standards. (Item 1A, Item 7) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "The costs to comply with environmental laws and regulations could have a material effect on". Position: milieu Item 1A.
risks.summary: Environmental regulations and climate change can impact Duke Energy's energy strategy and asset values

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The availability and deployment of generation and grid technologies can impact Duke Energy's ability to achieve modernization and carbon reduction objectives. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "Duke Energy is subject to business, policy, regulatory, technology, economic and competitive uncertainties and contingencies". Position: haut Item 1A.
risks.summary: Technologies play a key role in Duke Energy's energy modernization strategy

risks.title: Nuclear Operations Risk
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy operates multiple nuclear facilities including McGuire, Oconee, Catawba, Robinson, Brunswick and Harris. Nuclear liability is capped by the Price-Anderson Act at approximately 16.3 billion dollars. Uninsured losses could materially impact operations. (Item 5) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "REGULATORY, LEGISLATIVE AND LEGAL RISKS The Duke Energy Registrants’ regulated utility revenues, earnings and results". Position: haut Item 1A.
risks.summary: Nuclear operations represent significant liability and regulatory exposure

risks.title: Business Strategy Implementation
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy's future results depend on successfully implementing its business strategy to provide reliable energy while maintaining low costs and balancing modernization with carbon reduction objectives amid regulatory uncertainties. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner). Citation: "Delays in obtaining any required environmental regulatory approvals, failure to obtain and comply with them". Position: milieu Item 1A.
risks.summary: Execution on strategic objectives is subject to business, policy, regulatory and economic uncertainties

company_description: Duke Energy Corporation, through its subsidiaries, operates as an energy company in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I); and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I). The EU&I segment generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity to customers in the Southeast and Midwest regions. It generates electricity through coal, hydroelectric, natural gas, oil, renewables, and nuclear fuel. This segment also engages in the wholesale of electricity to municipalities, electric cooperative utilities, and other load-serving entities. The GU&I segment distributes natural gas to customers in the residential, commercial, industrial, and power generation natural gas sectors; and invests in pipeline transmission projects, renewable natural gas projects, and natural gas storage facilities. The company was formerly known as Duke Energy Holding Corp. and changed its name to Duke Energy Corporation in April 2006. Duke Energy Corporation was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.
